chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a free man who falsely accuses a slave, he said: “He is to be questioned; if his mother was free, the prescribed hadd punishment is administered to him.”

key_terms.أُمُّهُ: his mother, whose status affects the ruling
key_terms.اَلْحُرِّ: a free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: falsely accuses or fabricates a slanderous claim
key_terms.يُسْأَلُ: his status is to be investigated or examined

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man falsely accuses a slave in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding false accusation against a mamluk. It indicates that the applicability of the hadd depends on the status of the slave’s mother, showing a juridical distinction relevant to lineage and legal protection in cases of slander.
